name: Date Caramel Mousse Cups
author: Carolina Gelen
description:
Mix together sticky dates, whipped cream and salty pretzels and you’ve got yourself a guaranteed crowd-pleaser. This no-bake sweet is as easy as dessert gets: Soak pitted dates in hot water while you use a food processor to whip some cream, then blend the dates into a smooth caramel and fold some into the cream. The result is a light date caramel mousse that’s rich and indulgent at the same time, ready to be scooped up into serving glasses. Pretzels play an important role in this recipe by not only bringing an inviting, crunchy texture to each bite, but also by balancing the sweetness with some savory and salty character.

Watch Carolina Gelen make this dish in this video.

ingredients.raw: 15 to 18 medium/300 grams whole Medjool dates
1 ¾ cups/446 grams plus ⅓ cup/86 grams heavy cream, divided
ingredients.item: cups/446 grams plus ⅓ cup/86 grams heavy cream

ingredients.raw: ¼ packed cup/59 grams light brown sugar
ingredients.item: packed cup/59 grams light brown sugar

steps.text: Split open each date and remove the pit. Add the pitted dates to a heat-proof bowl and cover with boiling water. Soak until softened, about 8 minutes.

Add 1¾ cups of cream to a food processor and whip to soft peaks, about 45 seconds. Scrape down the sides of the bowl and continue whipping for 20 to 30 seconds more, to medium-stiff peaks. Add the whipped cream to a mixing bowl.

Add the softened dates to a mesh strainer and allow the excess liquid to drain. Gently press the dates with a spatula to squeeze out any clinging liquid. In the same food processor bowl (no need to clean or wipe it), add the dates, brown sugar, vanilla and salt, and blend for 90 seconds, until smooth. Add the remaining ⅓ cup of cream and pulse until combined.

Add ½ cup/120 grams of date caramel purée to a piping bag (or skip the piping bag and follow the instructions in the next step). Add the remaining date caramel to the whipped cream and fold, using a flexible silicone spatula, until combined.

Pipe or spoon swirls of date caramel against the inside of six (8-ounce) dessert glasses, reserving some for topping. Divide the date whipped cream between the glasses (a heaping ½ cup in each) and top with remaining date caramel. Chill for at least 30 minutes (or up to 2 days), then serve garnished with whole and crushed pretzels. (Alternatively, the whip can be spread on a larger platter, chilled and then topped with pretzels before serving for a more transportable casserole-style dessert.)

name: David Liederman's Roast Chicken And Vegetables
author: Molly O’Neill

ingredients.raw: 4 carrots, peeled, cut in half lengthwise and then across
ingredients.preparation: peeled, cut in half lengthwise and then across

steps.text: Wash and dry the chicken well. In a shallow dish big enough to hold the chicken, combine the olive oil, garlic and thyme. Add the chicken and baste with the oil, garlic and thyme. Cover and refrigerate for at least 3 hours, and up to 24 hours, basting occasionally and turning to marinate evenly.

Ten minutes before cooking, preheat the oven to 450 degrees and remove the chicken from the refrigerator. Pour the marinade in a large cast-iron pan. Line the bottom of the pan with the carrot slices. Season the chicken inside and out with the salt and pepper and place on top of the carrots. Strew the onions and potatoes around the chicken. Place the pan in the oven and roast for 50 to 55 minutes, or until a meat thermometer reaches between 158 and 160 degrees when inserted in the thigh. Remove from the oven and allow the chicken to rest for 5 minutes before serving.
